whatItReplaces: The tracking report and 03 §14.2 quote `87.25` against `103.75` as `16 questions behind` for MR. Both are averages over four repetitions, and every plan row calls the comparison 'paired' while quoting the difference of two means: same run, not same question.

The two masks were added to the artifact for exactly this reading - the field's own docblock says a spread 'cannot separate one question flapping four times from four questions flapping once each'. Nothing in the repository read them until this tool.

A difference of means cannot say whether a 16-question gap is 16 questions the other arm wins every time, 16 questions nobody decides, or the residue of a much larger two-sided disagreement. On MR it is the third: the arms disagree on 29 and 8 of 121 questions in the first repetition.

MR.note: 17 durable misses and 4 durable wins are 13 of the 16.50; the remaining 3.5 is flapping asymmetry. Eight questions are wrong in both arms in every repetition, so no amount of resembling the reference pipeline wins them.

ceiling.note: The 84 the arm reports on the first repetition already contains the four durable wins. Closing every durable miss and losing nothing is 84 + 17 = 101/121 = 83.5%; closing them while losing the four wins — which is what 'become more like the reference arm' means, since those four are questions it loses in every repetition — is 84 + 13 = 97/121 = 80.2%. Both are below the 96/121 this campaign has been targeting, so the registered target was above the ceiling of the strategy that named it. Reaching 96 requires winning questions the reference arm also loses, which is a different class of work and is not on any current plan row.
ceiling.asymmetryWarning: Five of the six off-by-one misses are UNDER-counts and one is an over-count (2e6d26dc, 5 -> 6), and the aggregation class carries a second over-count (a9f6b44c, 2 -> 4). Any treatment that pushes the arm toward inclusion moves five questions up and may move two down, so the net of a purely directional fix is three at best. That constraint is stated before the experiment, not after.

whatItChanges: `16 questions behind` becomes `21, 18, 17, 10` by repetition, of which 13 is durable, 8 questions are lost in both arms, and 3.5 is the asymmetry of 18 flapping questions against 3.

The 96/121 target registered in `PREREG-MR-SESSION-CHANNEL` §5 was above the ceiling of matching the reference arm (97/121) and is retired with it. A target that a transplant cannot reach is not a target.

`MR is judge-limited` was already withdrawn (`§13.185`, `§13.186`) on the numeric channel; this reading removes the last place that annotation still applied, because the 16.50 it multiplied by 19.38% was never a paired count.
The MR work list becomes seventeen ids with a class each, not a capability with a deficit.
limits: The masks are per repetition, so a verdict is a property of the code only if the four repetitions share their prompt. On this artifact `promptVariants` is 1 for 500 of 500 questions, so they do; on an artifact where it is 4, `durable` would mean '_durable across four different prompts_' and would understate what a fix can reach.

`agreed-wrong` is a ceiling of the harness and not of the capability: a question both arms miss may be one a different prompt, window or reader wins. What the reading says is that resembling the reference arm cannot win it.

The census classes are read from the gold and the answer, which is `tools/mr-failure-census.mjs`'s classifier and shares its blindness: a wrong answer that keeps the gold's number is invisible, and a gold that spells its number is read from the first number in the sentence.

`feature.metrics.correct` is repetition 0 (419 of 419/417/425/427), so a reader who divides it by the question count reads one repetition of four. The tool says so at the top of its output because the artifact cannot: no field records which repetition the headline came from.
